_comment: Tier-2/tier-3 supporting data for hypotheses H1/H2/H3 (methodology.md sections 81.8/82 [H1], 83.5/83.6 [H2], 86.6/86.7 [H3], revised 87.5/87.6). NONE of this is a licensed anchor: it never feeds the published estimate, band, or site/data/hormuz.json (owner's 2026-11-16 tier-3 directive; GOVERNANCE.md 'read, don't scrape' for tier-2). It exists only so scripts/score_hypotheses.py has something concrete to score H2/H3 against. Research/CEO should append a new dated entry to the relevant list each cycle a new PortWatch/UKMTO/Kpler reading is logged in signal-log.md, rather than this script trying to fetch it itself (PortWatch's ArcGIS endpoint *could* be queried mechanically, but UKMTO/Kpler readings are read from news coverage by a person, per the standing 'read, don't scrape' rule, so this file is a manually-curated mirror of what is already in signal-log.md/methodology.md, not a new independent source).

h3_ukmto_weekly_transits.next_reading_status: Not yet out as of 2026-11-22 (75th cycle searched specifically and found none dated past 2026-11-20; methodology.md 87.5). h3_kpler_hormuz_flow_7day_ma._comment: Kpler's 7-day moving average of Hormuz oil transits PLUS Gulf-of-Oman ship-to-ship transfers, in million b/d. Kpler's own figure, self-labelled 'provisional'. This is the metric the 74th-cycle H3 finding (methodology.md 86.6) was built on.

readings.source: Bloomberg report republished by gCaptain, 'Iran Intensifies Hormuz Tanker Attacks Just as Oil Prices Slide' (19 Nov 2026), logged 74th cycle

h3_kpler_total_regional_exports._comment: A DIFFERENT Kpler metric -- total regional (Gulf) oil exports via ALL routes, not Hormuz-specific. Found 75th cycle (methodology.md 87.5) and explicitly flagged there as likely NOT comparable to h3_kpler_hormuz_flow_7day_ma above, even though both are 'Kpler' figures -- a concrete instance of the standing caution to check each Kpler figure's stated scope before treating two of its numbers as comparable. score_hypotheses.py keeps this as context only, never averaged or combined with the flow_7day_ma series above.

readings.source: Kpler's own blog explainer, kpler.com/blog/explainer-how-mideast-gulf-crude-exports-returned-to-pre-war-levels, read directly 75th cycle

Rudaw, quoting Kpler's Homayoun Falakshahi directly, logged 75th cycle (methodology.md 87.5); scope ('total exports') inferred by Research from Kpler's own Sept terminology, not stated explicitly in this source

h3_kpler_total_regional_exports.research_reconciliation_note: If the Sept bypass share (40%) held into November, 15.3 total implies roughly 9.2 Hormuz-specific -- close to both the 9.1 EIA 3Q26 anchor and the flow_7day_ma series' low end (~10.0), i.e. plausibly NOT in conflict with either, but this is Research's own unverified arithmetic (methodology.md 87.5), not a confirmed figure. Net effect: downgrades H3 from 'two independent sources agreeing' to 'one primary raw count (UKMTO) in real decline, ambiguously corroborated by a commercial provider whose other same-month figure reads as recovery.'

h3_iea_context._comment: IEA (International Energy Agency) November 2026 Oil Market Report figures, found 75th cycle (methodology.md 87.5) -- context for H3, not a Hormuz-specific transit figure, logged because it points toward continued recovery through October, in tension with a clean 'declining in November' reading.
